provenance.source: Structural-trajectory region/sector concordance: EXIOBASE coarse-v3 build labels → the trajectory's development/composition archetypes (World Bank income groupings for regions; ISIC/EU KLEMS goods-vs-services split for sectors)
provenance.licence: derived mapping (CC BY 4.0); underlying groupings: World Bank income classification (CC BY 4.0), EU KLEMS/ISIC industry taxonomy
provenance.notes: Maps each real EXIOBASE coarse-v3 build label onto one of the structural trajectory's archetype keys, so a real build's actual regions/sectors carry a documented, differentiated trajectory instead of every label falling through to the global __all__ default (review P1c 2026-08-28). Regions map to N (advanced/high-income proxy) or S (emerging/developing proxy) by World Bank income grouping. Sectors map to BRD (goods-producing: the trajectory's above-average productivity-growth, carbon-intensive archetype) or MIL (services/mixed: below-average productivity, lighter carbon intensity) by the standard goods-vs-services ISIC split. The archetype trajectories themselves live in trajectories_v1.json; this file is the reviewable bridge (like the Phase-6 ENCORE concordance). A label not listed here is reported by the loader's validation as an unmapped fallthrough rather than silently taking __all__.

sources.region_archetype: World Bank country and lending groups (income classification) — high-income economies → N (advanced proxy), low/middle-income → S (emerging proxy). https://datahelpdesk.worldbank.org/knowledgebase/articles/906519
sources.sector_archetype: ISIC Rev.4 goods-vs-services split / EU KLEMS industry taxonomy — goods-producing industries (agriculture, extraction, energy, manufacturing, construction) → BRD; distribution, transport and services → MIL. https://unstats.un.org/unsd/classifications/Econ/isic
